questions.question: When two straight lines intersect, what is the geometric relationship between vertically opposite angles?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles formed by two intersecting lines are always equal in measure (angle a = angle c and angle b = angle d).

questions.question: Two adjacent angles that lie on a straight line and sum to 180° form a ____.
questions.explanation: By definition, adjacent angles on a straight line form a linear pair and are supplementary.

questions.question: Two intersecting lines form angle x and angle y as a linear pair. If x = 2y, calculate the measures of x and y.
questions.explanation: Linear pair sum: x + y = 180°. Substitute x = 2y: 2y + y = 180° => 3y = 180° => y = 60°. Then x = 2(60°) = 120°.

questions.question: If two lines intersect and one angle measures 35°, prove the measures of all remaining three angles with geometric reasons.
questions.explanation: Let angle a = 35°. 1. Angle b forms a linear pair with a: b = 180° - 35° = 145° (Linear Pair Postulate). 2. Angle c is vertically opposite to a: c = a = 35° (Vertically Opposite Angle Theorem). 3. Angle d is vertically opposite to b: d = b = 145° (Vertically Opposite Angle Theorem). Thus, the four angles are 35°, 145°, 35°, and 145°.
